items.question: Solve x² − 5x − 14 = 0. Show your algebra and check both roots.
items.solution: Find two numbers with product −14 and sum −5: −7 and 2. Factor x²−5x−14=(x−7)(x+2). By the zero-product rule x=7 or x=−2. Checks: 49−35−14=0 and 4+10−14=0.

criteria.description: Use (x−7)(x+2) or a correct equivalent root-finding method.
criteria.missingFeedback: Find two numbers with product −14 and sum −5.

criteria.description: Set both linear factors to zero or use the equivalent quadratic method.
criteria.missingFeedback: Set each factor equal to zero; do not set only the whole expression equal to zero.

criteria.description: State x=7 and x=−2 with signs correct.
criteria.missingFeedback: Check both roots by substitution into the original equation.

items.question: In a survey of 250 learners, 32% chose walking as their main route to school. Calculate how many learners chose walking. Show a method.
items.solution: 32%=32/100=0.32. Therefore 0.32×250=80 learners. Alternatively, 10%=25 so 30%=75 and 2%=5, giving 80.

criteria.missingFeedback: Convert the percentage to a proportion of the whole.
Apply the percentage to all 250 learners, not just to 32.

criteria.description: Obtain 80 learners with the unit indicated.
criteria.missingFeedback: Check that the result is less than 250 and close to one third.

items.question: Find the general indefinite integral of 6x² − 4x + 3 with respect to x. Include the constant of integration.
items.solution: Integrate each term: ∫6x² dx=2x³, ∫−4x dx=−2x², ∫3 dx=3x. Therefore F(x)=2x³−2x²+3x+C. Check by differentiating F to obtain 6x²−4x+3.

criteria.description: Integrate at least one non-constant power term using n+1 in the exponent.
criteria.missingFeedback: Increase the power by one and divide by the new exponent.
Differentiate your cubic term; it should return 6x².
Check the negative sign and coefficient by differentiation.
Remember the constant integrates to 3x, and indefinite integrals need +C.

items.question: Solve z² + 4z + 13 = 0 over the complex numbers. Give both solutions in a + bi form.
items.solution: Discriminant b²−4ac=16−52=−36. Quadratic formula z=(−4±√(−36))/2=(−4±6i)/2=−2±3i. Check (z+2)²=−9 for both.

criteria.missingFeedback: Use b²−4ac and preserve the negative sign.
Use √(−36)=6i and keep both ± branches.

criteria.description: Obtain real part −2 in both roots.
criteria.missingFeedback: Divide the entire numerator by 2.
Use both signs of the square root and check by substitution.

items.topic: Calculus: stationary points and mathematical justification
items.question: For f(x)=x³−3x, find the two stationary points and classify them as local maxima or minima. Explain your reasoning.
items.solution: f′(x)=3x²−3=3(x²−1), so stationary x-values are −1 and 1. f(−1)=2 and f(1)=−2. f′′(x)=6x, so f′′(−1)=−6<0 gives local maximum (−1,2), and f′′(1)=6>0 gives local minimum (1,−2).

criteria.description: Obtain f′(x)=3x²−3 and set it to zero.
criteria.missingFeedback: Differentiate first, then set the gradient equal to zero.
Solve x²−1=0 carefully and state both signs.

criteria.description: Substitute stationary x-values into f and use the second derivative or equivalent sign analysis.
criteria.missingFeedback: Use the original function for y-values and f′′ or sign changes for classification.
Substitute each x-value into f, not f′.

criteria.description: Explain why f′′(−1)<0 implies a maximum and f′′(1)>0 implies a minimum, or equivalent gradient changes.
criteria.missingFeedback: Make the classification follow from a valid derivative sign argument.

items.question: Five study-session times in minutes are 4, 6, 6, 8 and 11. Find the mean and median, then explain which measure is larger and by how much.
items.solution: The total is 4+6+6+8+11=35, so the mean is 35/5=7 minutes. The values are ordered, and the middle (third) value is 6 minutes, the median. Thus the mean is 1 minute larger than the median.

criteria.missingFeedback: Add all five values, including both 6s.
Divide by the number of observations, not by their sum.

criteria.description: Identify the third of five ordered observations as the median position.
criteria.missingFeedback: Order the data and locate the middle observation.
Do not confuse the middle value with the mean.

criteria.description: Explain that mean (7) exceeds median (6) by 1 minute.
criteria.missingFeedback: State the direction of the comparison and its numerical difference.

items.question: The equation x²−5x+6=0 has two roots p and q. What is 1/p+1/q?
items.solution: p+q=5 and pq=6 by Vieta’s formulas. Therefore 1/p+1/q=(p+q)/(pq)=5/6. Alternatively p=2 and q=3, so 1/2+1/3=5/6. Only C is correct.

items.question: For real x, statement P is x²>4 and statement Q is |x|>2. Which claim is true?
items.solution: For real x, x²>4 is equivalent to |x|²>2². Both sides are nonnegative, so taking square roots gives |x|>2. Conversely |x|>2 implies x²>4. Therefore P if and only if Q; answer C.

choices.text: P implies Q but Q does not imply P
Q implies P but P does not imply Q
P and Q are logically equivalent
They are equivalent only for x>0
